original_interpretation: SEMI P39 (OASIS) defines an interchange format for hierarchical integrated-circuit mask layout data and was created, from 2001, as a successor to GDSII Stream, which had been the de facto layout-interchange standard for more than two decades.
evidence_found: "The purpose of this Specification is to define an interchange and encapsulation format for hierarchical integrated circuit mask layout information." "In the fall of 2001, SEMI's Data Path Task Force formed a working group to define a successor to the venerable GDSII Stream format, which had served the I.C. industry as a de facto standard for layout interchange for more than two decades." (SEMI P39 store page, Abstract)

original_interpretation: SEMI's P39 background states that GDSII Stream was limited by 16-bit and 32-bit integer fields, inefficient geometry representation and high structural overhead, with file sizes in some cases reaching many tens of gigabytes; OASIS was chartered to achieve at least an order-of-magnitude file-size improvement and full 64-bit capability.
evidence_found: "The old format, limited by 16-bit and 32-bit internal integer fields, by its inefficient representation of cell-native geometric figures, and by high structural overhead ... file sizes were becoming unwieldy, in some cases growing to many tens of gigabytes." Goals: "Achieve at least an order-of-magnitude file size improvement compared to GDSII Stream." "make the new format fully 64-bit capable." (SEMI P39 Abstract, Background)

original_interpretation: Under NIST's CHIPS guardrails final rule (15 CFR Part 231), the Expansion Clawback runs for ten years from the award date, while the Technology Clawback's term is set per award in the award documents, and it bars only knowing joint research or technology licensing with a foreign entity of concern on technologies the Secretary has flagged as raising national security concerns.
evidence_found: §231.202(a): "During the 10-year period beginning on the date of the award ... may not engage in any significant transaction involving the material expansion of semiconductor manufacturing capacity in a foreign country of concern"; 231.102 response: "CPO is removing the definition of applicable term from the rule and will instead articulate the applicable term of a particular award in the relevant award documents."; Technology Clawback "prohibits the covered entity from knowingly engaging in any joint research or technology licensing effort with a foreign entity of concern that relates to a technology or product that raises national security concerns as determined by the Secretary" (88 FR 65600)
